I can't query the NAS-Bench-201 tables from here, so these are priors from the benchmark's general structure. Replacing a strong op like conv3x3 with a weak one usually costs more than replacing none, and adding an op to a none edge usually gains more than adding it to a conv. Cross-dataset consistency with a practical margin is a strict bar, so most claims get low numbers.
